One week ago, federal officers at the nation’s busiest commercial border crossing stopped a truckload of salt — and pulled out more than $30 million in methamphetamine.

According to FreightWaves’ reporting, the October 12 seizure happened at Laredo’s World Trade Bridge when a Customs and Border Protection officer flagged a 2020 International LT625 tractor-trailer whose cargo was listed as salt for a secondary inspection. Nonintrusive imaging turned up anomalies, and a physical search found 76 bags holding 3,395.91 pounds of suspected methamphetamine concealed in the commodity. CBP’s own news release puts the street value at $30,355,444.

The drugs were seized. The driver, the tractor and the trailer were released. Homeland Security Investigations is now running the case.

Here is what federal authorities will not say: who the trucking company was, where it was registered, who the importer of record was, where the shipment was bound — and why the driver walked free. FreightWaves put those questions directly to CBP and HSI; both declined to answer, citing the ongoing investigation.

“This successful enforcement action underscores our resolve to protect our communities from dangerous contraband,” said Laredo Port Director Alberto Flores in the release.

That silence is worth watching. Laredo is the busiest commercial land port in the United States, handling 2.95 million inbound truck crossings from Mexico in 2025, according to federal transportation data cited by FreightWaves. In a river of freight that wide, ordinary cargo makes the best camouflage — just last month, federal investigators pulled more than 2,000 pounds of methamphetamine out of a cabbage shipment in South Texas. Salt, cabbage: the cover loads change; the playbook doesn’t.

The pattern keeps three watchdog questions on the board: was the driver an unwitting hauler or part of the operation? Who booked the load, and who was waiting for it on the other side? And what happens at the next secondary inspection, when the last one produced a $30 million find and no names?

For now, the public record shows a record-scale seizure and a released driver. Webb Watch 956 will keep watching the HSI investigation — and the questions nobody has answered yet.

excerpt: CBP officers found 3,395 pounds of suspected methamphetamine hidden in a truck manifested as salt at the World Trade Bridge. The drugs were seized — the driver, tractor and trailer were released. CBP and HSI won't say who the carrier was or where the load was headed.
title: $30.4 Million in Meth, Buried in Salt: The World Trade Bridge Bust and the Questions Still Unanswered
